title: Functorial Finsupp coordinates for constant coefficients modulo p
statement: Let X and Y be qcqs schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], g:Y→X any scheme morphism, Λ any commutative ring in Type(u+1), p a prime and q any natural number. There exist an index type I in Type(u+1) and additive equivalences identifying H^q(X,constant Λ/(p)) [def-sc-constant-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] with I→₀H^q(X,constant Z/p), and H^q(Y,g^*constant Λ/(p)) with I→₀H^q(Y,g^*constant Z/p). Under these equivalences the cohomology pullback acts on each coordinate by the pullback for constant Z/p. There is no field, characteristic, smoothness, connectedness or properness hypothesis, and no Frobenius model in this statement.

source.place: filtered-colimit continuity, with Tag 0739 and the explicit basis construction of lem-sc-constant-mod-charp-finite-sum-colimit

proof.text: Use the canonical ULift(ZMod p)-module structure on Λ/(p) and choose a basis I. Repeat the explicit basis and finite-subcoproduct construction in the proof of the coefficient presentation theorem, retaining the chosen summand inclusions. This identifies the underlying constant sheaf with an I-indexed coproduct of X.constantZMod p. Pullback preserves this coproduct and its finite-subcoproduct diagram.

Apply large-universe filtered-colimit continuity to X and Y and additive preservation of finite biproducts by Sheaf.functorH. The colimit of the finite sums of cohomology groups is their Finsupp direct sum, giving a and b for the same I.

Naturality of Etale.cohomologyMap with respect to each summand inclusion gives the equation on single-coordinate classes. Every Finsupp is a finite sum of these classes, so additivity proves the equation for all x and i. An empty basis makes both direct sums zero.
